answer: Proof-of-work bonding makes each agent identity cost real compute before it can vote. An agent joins by finding a hash whose leading bits form a hard vertex and then locks a stake that scales with every peer it claims. A thousand noisy clones can start a ripple of cheap signups, but each must pay its own bond, so the ring's total spend grows linearly while peer review buys no credit. Reputation decays unless independent reviewers sign, and a caught cluster forfeits its bonds, making a Sybil swarm cost more than the single walnut of reward it could ever farm.
